steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Component 2 examines Global Film, requiring knowledge of set non-English language films and the ability to analyse and compare them.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Section A focuses on a non-English language European film, testing analysis of film language, representation and cultural context.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Section B focuses on a second non-English language film from outside Europe, testing similar skills with additional emphasis on global contexts.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Comparative analysis is central to Component 2: you must be able to discuss similarities and differences between your two set global films.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Use point-by-point comparison throughout your essay rather than discussing each film separately and adding comparison at the end. Balance your discussion of both films equally: the mark scheme rewards equal attention to each set film. Always connect cultural context to specific film language choices rather than providing isolated background information. Use comparative connectives explicitly: 'similarly,' 'by contrast,' 'whereas,' 'while Film A does X, Film B does Y' to make your comparison clear. Acknowledge your own cultural position as a UK viewer and consider how this affects your interpretation of each global film.
